title: Vernal Awakening (Ka Pyrem)
cultural_context: A beloved lyrical celebration of Spring in Meghalaya. Describes the awakening of mountain flora, the blooming of the pink Himalayan cherry blossoms (tiew-doh-maw) and wild yellow orchids (tiew-pathaw), the playful calling of the forest cuckoo, and the renewal of love and hope in highland villages.
lyrics_khasi:
Ha ki riat ba rben ki syntiew ki phuh,
Ka Pyrem ka la wan ban pynkmen ia ngi!
U tiew-doh-maw u la pynpaw la ka khmat,
Ka sngi ka la shai ha ka dur ba phyrnai.

Ki sim-tyngwieng ki rwai ha ki tnat dieng,
Ka lyer-pyrem ka beh ha ka sur ba bang;
Ko samla ba shlur, to mih noh sha rep,
Ba ka ri kan ai ia ka spah ba paka!
lyrics_english:
Along the steep rocky gorges the mountain flowers bloom,
Sweet Spring has arrived to gladden our hearts!
The wild rock orchid reveals its radiant face,
The morning sun shines in brilliant resplendence.

The swallows warble upon leafy branches,
The gentle spring breeze wafts in delicious sweetness;
O brave young cultivators, go forth unto the fields,
That our beloved homeland may yield her richest bounty!

stanzas.title: Ka Jingphuh ki Syntiew (Blossoming of Flowers)
stanzas.khasi:
Ha ki riat ba rben ki syntiew ki phuh,
Ka Pyrem ka la wan ban pynkmen ia ngi!
U tiew-doh-maw u la pynpaw la ka khmat,
Ka sngi ka la shai ha ka dur ba phyrnai.
stanzas.english: In deep gorges blossoms awaken; Spring arrives bringing joy! Rock orchids unveil their faces, the sun shines in sparkling radiance.

stanzas.title: Ka Sur ka Lyer-Pyrem (Melody of the Spring Wind)
stanzas.khasi:
Ki sim-tyngwieng ki rwai ha ki tnat dieng,
Ka lyer-pyrem ka beh ha ka sur ba bang;
Ko samla ba shlur, to mih noh sha rep,
Ba ka ri kan ai ia ka spah ba paka!
stanzas.english: Swallows sing on high tree limbs; spring breezes blow sweet. Rise up, valiant youth, to cultivate the land for bountiful harvest!

vocabulary.tiew-doh-maw: Native wild epiphytic orchid clinging to mossy mountain rocks
vocabulary.sim-tyngwieng: Highland swallow or swift bird darting across river ravines
vocabulary.lyer-pyrem: Gentle vernal breeze carrying forest flower pollen
vocabulary.riat ba rben: Deep, heavily forested highland ravine or limestone canyon
